precepts.text: If ye love me, keep my commandments. That's the love they don't want.
precepts.point: That verse speaks volumes. Deceivableness: the easy word is deceit. Unrighteousness: sin. All deceit of sin, breaking God's laws. In them that perish, because they received not the love of the truth: this is about our people.

note.label: Drowning in Sin & Perdition

precepts.why:
2 Thessalonians 2:10 speaks of “all deceivableness of unrighteousness in them that perish; because they received not the love of the truth, that they might be saved.” That verse speaks volumes. Deceivableness, the easy word is deceit. Unrighteousness is sin. All the deceit of sin, breaking God's laws, in them that perish. This is about our people.

So what is the love they received not? Christ said it: “If ye love me, keep my commandments.” That's the love they don't want.

That is why the teaching in the churches is blasphemous. When they say God's laws are done away with, that's blasphemy, and the white man taught them that: the Catholic Church, then the Protestant church picked it up and pushes it worldwide.

precepts.text: Philip said, Lord, shew us the Father. Christ answered, have I been so long time with you, and yet hast thou not known me, Philip? He that hath seen me hath seen the Father. What is he telling Philip? I created you; I am your everlasting Father; you were brought forth through me.
precepts.point: Of the increase of his government and peace there shall be no end. It behooves us to learn God's laws, commandments, and statutes, because to set up a government you need everything we read at the beginning of class about what a community consists of. God's laws are going to filter everything for us. And we have to learn to think bigger: not a house, not property; the world is ours. In order for the world to be ours, we have to be able to set up all of those things.

note.label: The Negro Community: A Wasteland of Tears

precepts.why:
Isaiah calls the son that is given “The everlasting Father.” Most Christians, and even some Israelites, cannot explain that, because they have not figured out that the everlasting Father in the Old Testament was Christ. They say we always spoke to the Father. No, you did not speak to the Father; you spoke to Christ. That is why he is called the everlasting Father. John 14 is a precept for it.

“Philip saith unto him, Lord, shew us the Father, and it sufficeth us.” See Christ’s response: “Jesus saith unto him, Have I been so long time with you, and yet hast thou not known me, Philip? he that hath seen me hath seen the Father; and how sayest thou then, Shew us the Father?”

Yes, Christ looks like his Father. But what is he actually telling Philip? I created you. I am your Father, your everlasting Father. You were brought forth through me.

Remember, Christ is the only begotten of the Father. That means the Father created only Christ, and then told Christ to create everything else. So when Isaiah names the child born unto us “The mighty God, The everlasting Father”, it is because everything that exists was brought forth through him. That is why Philip, who had been with him so long, should have known him.

precepts.text: The way: he that saith he abideth in him ought himself also so to walk, even as he walked.
precepts.point: I am the way, the truth, and the life: no man cometh unto the Father, but by me.

note.label: Daily Bread for a Dying Man

precepts.why:
Christ says, “I am the way, the truth, and the life.” This goes into the bread of life: everything that happened with the manna was always symbolic of Christ, a shadow foreshadowing him. And the first thing he calls himself is the way.

John tells us what it means for Christ to be the way: “He that saith he abideth in him ought himself also so to walk, even as he walked.” We have to walk as he walked.

Christ is not a way you only talk about or feel; he is a path you walk. Whoever says he abides in Christ has to walk the same way Christ walked, in the same commandments, day by day. That is what it means to feed on him as the bread from heaven: to take in his word every day and live the way he lived.

precepts.text: The truth: thy law is the truth. He is the embodiment of it; he fulfilled and will fulfil all prophecies. Lo, I come: in the volume of the book it is written of me.
precepts.point: I am the way, the truth, and the life: no man cometh unto the Father, but by me.

note.label: Daily Bread for a Dying Man

precepts.why:
Christ says he is also “the truth.” The psalm says what the truth is: “Thy righteousness is an everlasting righteousness, and thy law is the truth.”

God's law is the truth, and Christ is the embodiment of all these things. He fulfilled, and will fulfil, all the prophecies: he came in the volume of the book, as it was written of him.

So when Christ says, I am the truth, he is saying he is the law of God walking in the flesh. Everything from beginning to end has Christ in it, which is why the Old Testament established everything else, and why we need here a little and there a little to unlock the scriptures. To come to the Father by Christ is to come by the truth, his everlasting righteousness and his law.

precepts.text: The life: whosoever drinketh of the water that I shall give him shall never thirst; it shall be in him a well of water springing up into everlasting life. That sustenance again: in 1 Corinthians 10 they all drank of that same spiritual drink.
precepts.point: I am the way, the truth, and the life: no man cometh unto the Father, but by me.

note.label: Daily Bread for a Dying Man

precepts.why:
Christ says he is “the life.” He tells the woman at the well: “But whosoever drinketh of the water that I shall give him shall never thirst; but the water that I shall give him shall be in him a well of water springing up into everlasting life.”

He is that sustenance again. Just as he said, “he that believeth on me shall never thirst”, he is the water as well as the bread. Remember in 1 Corinthians 10 it says they all ate the same spiritual meat and all drank of that same spiritual drink, from the spiritual rock in the wilderness.

The water out of the rock physically happened so that they could live, and so that we could have its meaning today. The water Christ gives becomes a well inside you, springing up into everlasting life. That is why he is the life.

precepts.text: The record that God gave of his Son is the whole Bible, starting in the Old Testament. At the time these letters were written, much of the New Testament was not there yet; the record was the Old Testament. The manna, the cloud, the rock, the water that came out of it so they could live: it physically happened so that we could have that today. He that hath the Son hath life: that is the bread, the sustenance from heaven.
precepts.point: I am the way, the truth, and the life: no man cometh unto the Father, but by me.

note.label: Daily Bread for a Dying Man

precepts.why:
“He that believeth on the Son of God hath the witness in himself: he that believeth not God hath made him a liar; because he believeth not the record that God gave of his Son.” Christians stop and say this record is exclusively the New Testament. No. The record that God gave of his Son is the whole Bible, starting in the Old Testament.

At the time these letters were written, maybe they had the gospels at best, but a lot of the New Testament was not there. So where do you find the record God gave? In the Old Testament: the manna, the cloud, the rock, the water that came out of it so that they could live. It physically happened so that we could have that today.

“And this is the record, that God hath given to us eternal life, and this life is in his Son.” That is the daily bread, the daily nourishment. “He that hath the Son hath life”: that is the bread, the sustenance from heaven, the Holy Spirit. “and he that hath not the Son of God hath not life.”

So it is not just, oh, I accept Christ, and that's all. It is everything we have read up to this point and everything in the Bible in its totality. That is the life Christ means when he says, I am the life.

precepts.text: I am the door: by me if any man enter in, he shall be saved, and shall go in and out, and find pasture. You want to get to the Most High? You enter in through Christ.
precepts.point: I am the way, the truth, and the life: no man cometh unto the Father, but by me.

note.label: Daily Bread for a Dying Man

precepts.why:
The last part of John 14:6 is “no man cometh unto the Father, but by me.” By Christ we know the Father. He says it another way: “I am the door: by me if any man enter in, he shall be saved.”

He is that door. You want to get to the Most High? You have to enter in through Christ, and whoever enters by him shall be saved.

“and shall go in and out, and find pasture.” He shall go in and out and find pasture, and find that rest. The door is the only way in to the Father, and on the other side of it is the pasture and the rest the sheep are fed with. That is how the bread from heaven feeds a dying man: by coming through Christ.

precepts.text: There is one God, and one mediator between God and men, the man Christ Jesus.
precepts.point: I am the way, the truth, and the life: no man cometh unto the Father, but by me.

note.label: Daily Bread for a Dying Man

precepts.why:
Christ says, “no man cometh unto the Father, but by me.” Paul says the same: “For there is one God, and one mediator between God and men, the man Christ Jesus.”

He is the life. There is one God and one mediator between God and men, and that mediator is the man Christ Jesus. Nobody else stands between us and the Father: not a priest, not a saint, not anybody else.

That is why he is the way, the truth and the life, the manna from heaven and the door. The flesh is dying, the mind forgets, and the inward man has to be renewed daily by the word. The only way that renewing reaches us from the Father is through the one mediator, the man Christ Jesus.

precepts.text: At that day ye shall know that I am in my Father, and ye in me, and I in you. Christ does what his Father tells him to do, and Christ tells us what to do, and we keep those commandments; all of them, not picking and choosing and cherry picking like Christians. He that hath my commandments, and keepeth them, he it is that loveth me; and I will love him, and will manifest myself to him. He is explaining how you receive the Holy Spirit: in order to have the Holy Spirit, you must be one with the Most High and his son.
precepts.point: Hear, O Israel: the Lord our God is one Lord. We start with the order first. We as a body have to be one, in unison, in sync. This is why we have been able to accomplish the amazing things we have in this congregation: because we are one.

note.label: Member's In The Body

precepts.why:
Christ warned of his departure, when he would no longer be with them in the body: “At that day ye shall know that I am in my Father, and ye in me, and I in you.” What does it mean? Christ does what his Father tells him to do, Christ comes and tells us what to do, and we keep those commandments.

“He that hath my commandments, and keepeth them, he it is that loveth me.” What commandments? The Father's commandments, all of them. We ain't Christians up in here picking and choosing and cherry picking, hopping and skipping around. Everything the Father told us to do: those are the commandments. The one who has them and keeps them is the man or woman that loves Christ, that loves the Lord.

“and he that loveth me shall be loved of my Father, and I will love him, and will manifest myself to him.” He is explaining the manifestation, how you receive the Holy Spirit. In order to have the Holy Spirit, you must be one with the Most High God and his Son.

That is how we keep the first commandment, to “love the Lord thy God with all thine heart, and with all thy soul, and with all thy might”: by keeping his commandments, and being one with the Father and the Son as they are one.

note.label: Recovering the Remnant: Worldwide Blitz

The Comforter, the Holy Ghost, “shall teach you all things, and bring all things to your remembrance, whatsoever I have said unto you.” Why would we need to remember the things Christ said? Because we would be made to forget. Through slavery the nations annihilated our twelve tribes, burned our records and beat us into submission, and we forgot what Christ said.

What did he say? That he would gather his elect from the four corners of the earth. That he was sent only to the lost sheep of the house of Israel. And: “If ye love me, keep my commandments.”

The Holy Spirit causes us to remember these things. If you don't remember them, you don't have the Holy Spirit on you. Keeping the commandments is the love Christ asks for, and the Spirit brings back to our remembrance who we are and what he said.

That is what is happening now: brothers and sisters waking up worldwide. Isaiah 44 promised it to Jacob, whom the Lord chose: “I will pour water upon him that is thirsty”, the word upon those thirsty for the truth, and “I will pour my spirit upon thy seed, and my blessing upon thine offspring: And they shall spring up as among the grass”. The Israelites are springing up worldwide like grass.

Who is that Comforter? “Even the Spirit of truth; whom the world cannot receive, because it seeth him not, neither knoweth him: but ye know him; for he dwelleth with you, and shall be in you.” Then Christ says, “I will not leave you comfortless: I will come to you.” He is letting us know he is the Comforter. precepts.text: I am the way, the truth, and the life: no man cometh unto the Father, but by me.
precepts.point: Demetrius the silversmith made shrines for Diana and stirred up the craftsmen because Paul had persuaded much people that they be no gods which are made with hands, endangering both their wealth and the temple of the great goddess whom all Asia worshipped.

note.label: The Iranians & The Ephesians

precepts.why:
“And the same time there arose no small stir about that way.” What way is this? Christ answers it: “I am the way, the truth, and the life: no man cometh unto the Father, but by me.” The way that Ephesus was stirred up about, the thing that caused a huge commotion in that city, was Christ himself.

They had a problem with Christ because a whole city was given to witchcraft. Ephesus owed its fame to the temple of Diana, and the “curious arts” practised there were the magical arts of the Ephesian conjurers. When Paul came preaching Christ, “many that believed came, and confessed, and shewed their deeds”, and those who used curious arts brought their books of witchcraft together and burned them before all men, fifty thousand pieces of silver worth. “So mightily grew the word of God and prevailed.”

That is what stirred the city. Demetrius the silversmith, “which made silver shrines for Diana”, called the craftsmen together and told them “by this craft we have our wealth”, and that Paul had “persuaded and turned away much people, saying that they be no gods, which are made with hands.” People were repenting and turning away from their witchcraft, and that put both the craftsmen’s living and the temple of “the great goddess Diana” in danger. Diana, with all the breasts on her, goes into fertility: satanic worship at the end of the day.

So the stir “about that way” was a city given over to idolatry and sorcery fighting against Christ, the only way to the Father. There is no salvation without him, and the same call goes out to our people now: repent from the idolatry, the fornication and the lasciviousness, and come to the way.

precepts.text: If ye love me, keep my commandments, and the Comforter will teach you all things.
precepts.point: The natural man cannot receive or know the things of the Spirit.

note.label: The Kingdom Of Adam And The Old World

precepts.why:
“Eye hath not seen, nor ear heard, neither have entered into the heart of man, the things which God hath prepared for them that love him. But God hath revealed them unto us by his Spirit”. Who are those that love him? Christ said: “If ye love me, keep my commandments.”

There are two types of people in this world: people who say they love God, like the Christians who all say they love the Lord and love Jesus, and people who do what Jesus said. Which one is justified? If you are not doing what he said and you say you love him, you are a liar.

To the ones who keep his commandments he sends the Spirit: “And I will pray the Father, and he shall give you another Comforter, that he may abide with you for ever”. And: “But the Comforter, which is the Holy Ghost, whom the Father will send in my name, he shall teach you all things, and bring all things to your remembrance”. That is how we learn the different levels of understanding in the scriptures; it starts with the apostles, and they teach the people.

So we do not teach with man's wisdom from a theology school or seminary; we teach “which the Holy Ghost teacheth; comparing spiritual things with spiritual.” The things God has prepared for us, the holy city, living forever, being with Christ even if we die keeping the commandments, are on another level. They are freely given to us of God; we just have to keep his commandments.

precepts.text: In my Father's house are many mansions; the Most High has something far greater in store than the false security of this captivity.
precepts.point: So God led the people about, through the way of the wilderness of the Red Sea, and the children of Israel went up harnessed out of the land of Egypt.

note.label: Exodus 13: By Strength of Hand the Lord Brought Us Out

precepts.why:
Against the false security of Egypt, the Most High has something much greater in store. Christ says, “In my Father’s house are many mansions: if it were not so, I would have told you. I go to prepare a place for you.”

A little job, government assistance, a car and food from the store are the fish and the leeks of Egypt. What is prepared for Israel is the world, the earth, and many mansions in the Father's house. God led the people about through the wilderness so they would not trade that for Egypt, and the people in America who never want this kingdom to come down are holding on to Egypt when the Most High has far more in store for them.

Unless the Spirit of the Lord deals with you, you will never understand the Bible or the laws; that is why there was such contention between Christ and the Pharisees, for the Spirit had not revealed to them who he was.

Unless the Spirit of the Lord deals with you, you will never understand the Bible or the laws, this law of the meat offering included. That is why there was such contention between Christ and the Pharisees: the Spirit had not revealed to them who he was.

note.label: Numbers 29: The Feasts of the Seventh Month

precepts.why:
Moses told the children of Israel “according to all that the Lord commanded Moses.” Christ puts the same charge on us: “If ye love me, keep my commandments.” Keeping the set feasts is keeping his commandments.

With it comes a promise: “And I will pray the Father, and he shall give you another Comforter, that he may abide with you for ever; Even the Spirit of truth; whom the world cannot receive, because it seeth him not, neither knoweth him: but ye know him; for he dwelleth with you, and shall be in you.”

The world cannot receive that Spirit of truth, because it neither sees him nor knows him. Those who love Christ and keep his commandments know him, for he dwells with them. That spirit is how the feasts of the seventh month, and the sacrifices that went with them, are understood in these last days.

That spirit is how this truth is understood in these last days.

The knowing comes when it is sent. The word comes down in order, from the Most High to Christ, to the angels, and into our spirit when it is time to wake up. Until then, like Samuel, a man can be in the house and not yet know the Lord.

precepts.why:

The Father is greater than the Son. That is why, after all is subdued under his feet, Christ hands the kingdom to the Father. He is the son of man made a little lower than the angels and crowned with glory and honour, given dominion over the works of God's hands, yet the one who gave him that dominion is greater than he.

note.label: Jeremiah 32: Buying the Field of Redemption

precepts.why:
When the Lord gathers Israel out of all countries where he drove them, “I will give them one heart, and one way, that they may fear me for ever”. One heart and one way means one mind and full agreement. Christ says what that one way is: “I am the way, the truth, and the life: no man cometh unto the Father, but by me.”

There are no multiple ways and no multiple truths; there is one way to the Father, through the Son. That answers why Christianity has so many denominations: they are not walking in the one way. This is being seen today as we rise up and get understanding of who we are, our nationality, and our God being a black God for his people, a God who does not love all nations alike but will reward these nations for what they have done to us. He puts his fear in our hearts that we shall not depart from him, and plants us in the land with his whole heart and his whole soul.

precepts.text: If ye love me, keep my commandments, and the Comforter follows.
precepts.point: The Holy Ghost is bound to the law. To resist the Holy Ghost is to resist the commandments, and the Comforter brings the words of Christ to remembrance.

note.label: Matthew 3: John the Baptist and the Baptism of the Holy Ghost and Fire

precepts.why:
Christ says, “If ye love me, keep my commandments.” Keeping the commandments comes first, and the Comforter follows. The Holy Ghost is bound to the law: the one who loves Christ keeps his commandments, and to him the Comforter is sent.

This is the baptism John pointed to, with the Holy Ghost and with fire, and it is not given to those who resist the commandments.

precepts.text: The Comforter, which is the Holy Ghost, shall teach you all things and bring all things to your remembrance.
precepts.point: The Holy Ghost is bound to the law. To resist the Holy Ghost is to resist the commandments, and the Comforter brings the words of Christ to remembrance.

note.label: Matthew 3: John the Baptist and the Baptism of the Holy Ghost and Fire

precepts.why:
Christ tells what the Comforter does: “But the Comforter, which is the Holy Ghost, whom the Father will send in my name, he shall teach you all things, and bring all things to your remembrance, whatsoever I have said unto you.”

The Comforter is the Holy Ghost, and his work is to teach and to bring the words of Christ to remembrance. It comes after “If ye love me, keep my commandments.” So the baptism of the Holy Ghost that Christ gives is the Father sending the Comforter in Christ's name to those who keep his commandments, teaching them and bringing his words back to their minds.

precepts.text: The Comforter, which is the Holy Ghost, shall teach them all things and bring all things to their remembrance.
precepts.point: The Holy Ghost comes in an order that begins with the law: turn at his reproof and keep the commandments, and then he pours out his spirit and opens the understanding. Only the Most High can give the wisdom to interpret this book, which is the most purchased yet least understood book on the earth.

note.label: Acts 1: The Promise of the Father and the Kingdom Restored to Israel

precepts.why:
“But the Comforter, which is the Holy Ghost, whom the Father will send in my name, he shall teach you all things, and bring all things to your remembrance, whatsoever I have said unto you.”

Christ could teach only so much in three years, because a man can bear only so much. The Comforter would open their understanding in increments after his death, guiding them into all truth and bringing his words back to their remembrance. That is the promise of the Father they were told to wait for in Jerusalem.

precepts.text: The Comforter, the Holy Ghost, will teach all things and bring all things to remembrance, which is why we are reliving the restitution now.
precepts.point: The kingdom itself was taken by force, and Israel was led away captive into all nations, showing again that our people are the ones who lost it and must have it restored.

note.label: Acts 3: The Restitution of All Things

precepts.why:
The remembrance of Israel was made to cease, and Christ said how it comes back: “But the Comforter, which is the Holy Ghost, whom the Father will send in my name, he shall teach you all things, and bring all things to your remembrance, whatsoever I have said unto you.”

The Comforter teaches all things and brings all things to remembrance. That is why we are reliving the restitution now, before Christ comes: the remembrance that was lost is being brought back to our people through the Holy Ghost.

precepts.text: I am the way, the truth, and the life; no man cometh unto the Father but by me.
precepts.point: You cannot sneak into the kingdom through Islam, the Nation of Islam, Jehovah's Witnesses, Mormonism, Pentecostalism, Seventh-day Adventism, the Baptists, or Buddhism. Whoever climbs up some other way is a thief and a robber trying to sneak in without laboring; you must enter by the door, which is Christ.

note.label: Acts 4: The Stone the Builders Rejected

precepts.why:
Christ says it plainly: “I am the way, the truth, and the life: no man cometh unto the Father, but by me.”

No man comes to the Father any other way. That is why there is none other name under heaven given among men whereby we must be saved: not Moses, not Elias, not any other man or way.

precepts.text: Before the followers were called Christians at Antioch they were called This Way, because Christ said, I am the way, the truth, and the life; Saul persecuted this way unto the death.
precepts.point: Therefore they that were scattered abroad went every where preaching the word. Because of the great persecution the disciples had to flee, and our fathers were fugitives, always on the run, the way it was done to men like Nat Turner. It is going to come to that point again, where a brother might have to house a teacher whose name is on the news, wanted for sedition; you might be charged as guilty by association, but you have to see past it to protect your brother, because the gospel has to go forward. This is why we need such a high level of unity and love for one another to survive.

note.label: Acts 8: The Word Scattered Abroad, and the Baptism unto the Conscience

precepts.why: Before the followers were called Christians at Antioch, they were called This Way, because Christ said, “I am the way, the truth, and the life: no man cometh unto the Father, but by me.” Those scattered abroad preaching the word were this way, and it was this way that Saul persecuted unto the death.

precepts.text: Christ is the way, the truth, and the life, so those who followed him were called "this way."
precepts.point: Before the followers of Christ were called Christians in Acts 11, they were called "this way," meaning the way of Christ. Some people, when the persecution comes, will change their name back, stop wearing fringes, stop keeping the Sabbath, and hide, saying "that's not me."

note.label: Acts 9: A Chosen Vessel

precepts.why:
Before the followers of Christ were called Christians in Acts 11, they were called “this way”, meaning the way of Christ, because Christ said, “I am the way, the truth, and the life: no man cometh unto the Father, but by me.” That is who Saul was hunting with letters to Damascus: any of this way, whether men or women, to be brought bound unto Jerusalem.

This is why we tell brothers and sisters both to gird up their minds and build their faith by studying. When they notice you by your last name or your fringes, you will be persecuted. Some people, when the persecution comes, will change their name back, stop wearing fringes, stop keeping the Sabbath and hide, saying that's not me.

precepts.text: Jesus says, "I am the way, the truth, and the life," which is why the followers were called this way.
precepts.point: Before the followers of Christ were called Christians in Antioch, they were called "this way."

note.label: Acts 11: The Gentiles Are Scattered Israel

precepts.why:
“Jesus saith unto him, I am the way, the truth, and the life: no man cometh unto the Father, but by me.”

That is why the followers were called this way. Christ is the way, so those who followed him were the way, before they were called Christians first in Antioch.

note.label: Bishop Nathanyel | Revelation 4 Kingdom Vision

precepts.why:
The Comforter, the Holy Ghost sent by the Father in Christ's name, teaches all things and brings them to remembrance. Test a Christian's claim to have that Holy Ghost. After twenty, forty-six or sixty years, has it revealed that Christmas is a lie, that they are Israelites, or that they should not eat shrimp, crab, pork and swine?

If none of those things has been brought to remembrance, the claim does not match Christ's promise. You do not have the Holy Ghost; you have an unholy demon. The Comforter's teaching is shown by the understanding and remembrance of God's word, not merely announcing that you possess it.

note.label: Bishop Nathanyel | Revelation 3 A Message to The 7 Churches

precepts.why: I will come in to him, and will sup with him. What is that talking about? Repentance. Christ coming in and supping with you: when you are breaking bread, drinking wine, he is coming into your spirit, your mind, your heart, your soul, and supping with you; he is sharing the spiritual understanding with you. “Jesus answered and said unto him, If a man love me, he will keep my words: and my Father will love him, and we will come unto him,” And we will come unto him, “and make our abode with him.” We will make our abode with him. That means what? In your heart. The Lord is in your heart, in your soul, in your spirit.

moments.label: Daily Bread for a Dying Man
Escape Thankskilling : Oh God & My Lord

points: Some of us are coming out of those idolatry lifestyles. Whatever was an idol to you before this truth, it might not have been football, it could have been something else, it could have been your so-called boyfriend; all of it is idolatry, because you put it before the Lord.
Now we have the spirit of remembrance. We are coming back to our true heritage, knowing what we have to do to get the kingdom of God.

Whatever captivity we are in there is always an idol and always a trend of something. Before Rome it was the Greek captivity with four generals ruling in different parts, and the Olympics stem right back from the Greeks; the same thing happened at Ephesus when Paul cried out in the amphitheatre.

A lot of us slide back into it, and some envy one another. That is why we have to stay strong, stay focused, stay diligent and stay locked in: it is a fight, and we are warring for the hearts and the minds of our people.

Christ said he would gather his elect from the four winds; Christ said he was sent only to the lost sheep of the house of Israel; and Christ said, if ye love me, keep my commandments.

points: If ye love me, keep my commandments. Peace I leave with you, my peace I give unto you. Not the peace of the earth but peace of mind, and there is no price for peace of mind.
